checkpoints_not_frozen.why: written by the same run but NEVER evaluated -- 'best' under a different criterion, plus last/final. Excluded so no one can score one later and report it as this arm's result.

deliberate_deviations: Trained on OUR data: the three rhj_fewshot h5ads read in place through competitors/shared/occam_data.py, normalised log1p(counts / rowsum_FULL_PANEL * 10_000). STATE's own recipe reads a pre-normalised zarr. The FULL-panel denominator is what makes the 10,000 -> 2,000 emission map exact.

OUR 6,983-gene axis (hvg 6983), OUR splits, OUR per-(file, perturbation) exclusions. HepG2 splits three ways; jurkat and RPE1 are wholly training data -- the positive half of the few-shot design, since a perturbation held out of HepG2 still trains from the others.

cell_set_len 64 and hidden_dim 336, which are NOT the upstream config defaults (512 / 768). batch_encoder=True, which is non-default in EVERY in-repo upstream config. batch_size 64, lr 1e-3, max_steps 80000, val_freq 16000.

Checkpoint selected on val/celleval/selection_score = mean(pearson_delta, discrimination_score_l1) over the 103 HepG2 validation perturbations, mode=max. That is OUR selection metric, added by competitors/STATE/.../callbacks/validation_celleval.py; upstream's only live validation signal on this data was a loss on the TEST split.
Scored uncalibrated (model_nocal). No calibration and no NB emission for any competitor.

⚠️ 2 of 5 in-training validations were REFUSED by cell-eval for exceeding its log1p scale threshold (max 17.29 at step 32,000): the output head is a plain relu, non-negative but unbounded. The ceiling refusal was later removed on purpose (C26) since it would have discarded the arm over 1 value in 4.36M; this run predates that, so it selected from 3 of 5 validations. Its best, step 63,999, is the one frozen here.

Export-level fixes vs our first port (C27/S1+S2+S3), all making it MORE faithful, none touching training -- the checkpoint is unchanged and was NOT retrained: S1 ONE cell sentence per predict_step, because `padded=False` means 'this whole batch IS one sentence', so packing 4 sentences had been collapsing them into one 256-cell sentence in which ~8 perturbations attended to each other (the backbone is NoRoPE, so there was no length error and no warning); S2 no padding of short sentences, matching STATE's own _infer.py window `end = min(start + cell_set_len, len(idxs))` and its test sampler, which skips padding explicitly; S3 each cell's REAL batch covariate instead of one constant label broadcast over the panel, since batch_encoder=True adds its embedding to every token and a real 30-cell sentence spans 22 distinct batches. Together these moved the arm from 0.1306 (exactly the `meanpert` anchor) to 0.2362, and halved the across-split sd from 0.0050 to 0.0019.

export_fixes_this_number_depends_on.S1: one cell sentence per predict_step. padded=False means 'this batch IS one sentence', so 4 sentences were flattened into one 256-cell sentence spanning ~8-9 perturbations. Measured 52% change per cell.
export_fixes_this_number_depends_on.S2: no padding. STATE's inference runs a short sentence at its true length; tiling 30->64 cost a measured 7.2%.
export_fixes_this_number_depends_on.S3: per-cell batch covariate (56 distinct) instead of one constant, against a trained batch_encoder. Measured 0.37 relative change.
export_fixes_this_number_depends_on.net_effect: pearson_delta 0.1306 -> 0.2362, i.e. +0.1056, from export changes alone. The training was verified correct, so the checkpoint was never at fault.
